title: Representable sums and left-Kan acyclicity
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category and $R$ a commutative ring. Write $\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{op},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$; it is the module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for the constant ring on the topology generated by singleton identities [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Derived categories and cochain complexes mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $U\in\mathcal E$ and an $R$-module $M$, put $L_U(M)(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}M$, with restriction along $b:W\to V$ sending $(a,m)$ to $(ab,m)$. There are natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(L_U(M),H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,H(U))$, given by evaluation on the identity summand, with inverse $f\mapsto((a,m)\mapsto H(a)f(m))$. The functors $L_U$ are exact and take projective modules to projective presheaves, where projective means that every map out lifts across every epimorphism. Both $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}$ have enough projectives; specifically the map $\bigoplus_{U,x\in H(U)}L_U(R)\to H$, $(a,r)\mapsto rH(a)x$, is an epimorphism from a projective object. Small direct sums are exact and preserve projectivity in these categories. Let $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be any functor to another small category, $u_!$ the left adjoint to precomposition, and $C_{\mathcal E,R},C_{\mathcal D,R}$ the colimit functors [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose their total left derived functors have the canonical comparisons and are defined at every complex in the sense of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. Then $C_{\mathcal E,R}L_U(M)\cong M$ and $u_!L_U(M)\cong L_{uU}(M)$, naturally, with each generator sent identically on its coefficient. Every small sum $T=\bigoplus_cL_{U_c}(M_c)$, with arbitrary modules $M_c$, is left acyclic for both $C_{\mathcal E,R}$ and $u_!$: the canonical maps $LC_{\mathcal E,R}(T[0])\to C_{\mathcal E,R}(T)[0]$ and $Lu_!(T[0])\to u_!(T)[0]$ are isomorphisms. Also $u_!T=\bigoplus_cL_{uU_c}(M_c)$ is left $C_{\mathcal D,R}$-acyclic. For projective module resolutions $P_c\to M_c[0]$ vanishing in positive degrees, $\bigoplus_cL_{U_c}(P_c)\to T[0]$ is a projective resolution, and its images under $C_{\mathcal E,R}$ and $u_!$ are quasi-isomorphic respectively to $(\bigoplus_c M_c)[0]$ and $(\bigoplus_cL_{uU_c}(M_c))[0]$.

proof.text: Pointwise algebra. On the topology generated by identity coverings the sheaf equalizer condition is automatic, so every module presheaf is a sheaf. Thus [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives an abelian category with pointwise kernels and cokernels: sheafification does nothing. The same statement on the one-object identity category gives $\operatorname{Mod}_R$. In particular a morphism is epic exactly when every component is surjective, since its pointwise cokernel is zero exactly then. The direct sum [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], formed at each object, is a coproduct of presheaves: maps out are the unique linear maps prescribed on each summand, and their naturality is checked there. All indices are small in the fixed module universe.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable generators; arbitrary-coefficient refinement written explicitly by Q21.

proof.text: Exactness and lifting for sums. For a family of short exact module sequences, injectivity of the sum of the first maps follows componentwise. A finite-support element in the kernel of the sum of the second maps has, in each of its finitely many nonzero components, a preimage under the corresponding first map; these preimages give a finite-support preimage. Likewise a finite-support element of the last sum lifts using finitely many component lifts. This proves exactness of small sums in modules and, by Step 1, in presheaves. A map from a coproduct of projectives across an epimorphism lifts on each summand by projectivity; choosing those lifts and applying the coproduct universal property gives a lift on the sum. This proves preservation of projectivity in both categories.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable generators; arbitrary-coefficient refinement written explicitly by Q21.

proof.text: The evaluation adjunction. For $\theta:L_U(M)\to H$ define $f(m)=\theta_U(\mathrm{id}_U,m)$. Naturality along $a:V\to U$ gives $\theta_V(a,m)=H(a)f(m)$. Conversely this formula extends linearly from each summand to a natural transformation, since $H(b)H(a)=H(ab)$ for $b:W\to V$. Evaluation on the identity recovers $f$; the displayed formula recovers $\theta$. The formulas commute with postcomposition in $H$ and precomposition in $M$, giving exactly the claimed natural bijections.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable generators; arbitrary-coefficient refinement written explicitly by Q21.

proof.text: Exactness and projectivity of $L_U$. At $V$, the functor $L_U$ is a direct sum of copies of the input module indexed by $\operatorname{Hom}(V,U)$. Step 2 therefore proves its exactness. If $P$ is projective and $H\twoheadrightarrow H'$ is epic, Step 1 makes $H(U)\to H'(U)$ surjective. The module map $P\to H'(U)$ corresponding in Step 3 to a map $L_U(P)\to H'$ lifts to $H(U)$; the inverse bijection gives the required presheaf lift. Thus $L_U(P)$ is projective.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable generators; arbitrary-coefficient refinement written explicitly by Q21.

proof.text: Enough projectives, with the specified epimorphism. The module $R$ is projective: a linear map from $R$ is determined by the image of $1$, which lifts across any surjection. Hence $\bigoplus_{x\in M}R$ is projective by Step 2, and $(x,r)\mapsto rx$ is surjective since $m$ is the image of $(m,1)$. This gives enough projectives in modules. Steps 4 and 2 make $\bigoplus_{U,x\in H(U)}L_U(R)$ projective. Its map to $H$ is the sum of the natural transformations of Step 3 corresponding to $r\mapsto rx$. At $V$, any $y\in H(V)$ is the image of the identity summand with index $(V,y)$ and coefficient $1$. The map is therefore pointwise surjective, hence epic by Step 1. Its formula is exactly $(a,r)\mapsto rH(a)x$.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable generators; arbitrary-coefficient refinement written explicitly by Q21.

proof.text: Colimit of an induced presheaf. Write $C_{\mathcal E,R}$ for colimit over $\mathcal E^{op}$. The maps $L_U(M)(V)\to M$ sending every $(a,m)$ to $m$ form a cocone. Any cocone $\lambda_V:L_U(M)(V)\to N$ satisfies $\lambda_V(a,m)=\lambda_U(\mathrm{id}_U,m)$, by compatibility with restriction along $a$. Consequently it factors uniquely through the linear map $M\to N$, $m\mapsto\lambda_U(\mathrm{id}_U,m)$. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies $C_{\mathcal E,R}L_U(M)$ with $M$, with precisely the stated action on coefficients. The formula commutes with module maps, hence also with differentials when applied degreewise.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable generators; arbitrary-coefficient refinement written explicitly by Q21.

proof.text: Left Kan extension on an induced presheaf. Put $A=L_U(M)$, $B=L_{uU}(M)$ and let $\eta:A\to u^*u_!A$ be the adjunction unit. The map $t:A\to u^*B$, $(a,m)\mapsto(u(a),m)$, has adjoint $\alpha:u_!A\to B$. Step 3 applied on $\mathcal D$ gives $\beta:B\to u_!A$ from $m\mapsto\eta_U(\mathrm{id}_U,m)$. On the identity summand, $\alpha\beta$ sends $m$ to $m$, so Step 3 makes it $\mathrm{id}_B$. Under the Kan adjunction, $\beta\alpha$ corresponds to $u^*\beta\,t$. On $(a,m)$ this is the restriction along $u(a)$ of $\eta_U(\mathrm{id}_U,m)$, which is $\eta_V(a,m)$ by naturality of $\eta$. Thus $\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{u_!A}$. These inverse formulas give the claimed isomorphism, commute with coefficient maps and send the distinguished coefficient identically; all other summands follow by restriction.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable generators; arbitrary-coefficient refinement written explicitly by Q21.

proof.text: Right exactness and preservation of sums. Colimit is left adjoint to the constant-diagram functor: a map from the colimit is a compatible cocone, exactly a natural transformation to a constant presheaf. For either this adjunction or $u_!\dashv u^*$, the adjunction bijection identifies maps from the image of a coproduct with families of maps, and maps from the image of a cokernel with maps annihilating the preceding arrow. These are precisely the coproduct and cokernel universal properties, so both functors preserve small sums and cokernels. They preserve zero and finite biproducts, and hence addition of maps, since $f+g=\nabla(f\oplus g)\Delta$ and diagonals and codiagonals are specified by the biproduct identities. They are therefore additive and right exact, as required by the computation theorem. In particular Step 7 identifies $u_!T$ with $\bigoplus_cL_{uU_c}(M_c)$, via the coproduct inclusions.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), representable generators; arbitrary-coefficient refinement written explicitly by Q21.

proof.text: The actual projective resolutions and their images. By Step 5, the resolution-existence clause of [lem-trf-bounded-above-acyclic-derived-computation], applied to $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $M_c[0]$ with bound $0$, supplies $P_c\to M_c[0]$ zero in positive degrees. For any such supplied family, put $P=\bigoplus_cL_{U_c}(P_c)$ and let $a:P\to T[0]$ be the sum of its augmentations. Every $P^n$ is projective by Steps 4 and 2 and vanishes for $n>0$. Exactness in Steps 2 and 4 shows $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism: the augmented complexes remain exact, or equivalently their kernels modulo images are unchanged by those exact functors. Steps 6 and 8 identify $C_{\mathcal E,R}(P)$ with $\bigoplus_cP_c$ and its augmentation with $\bigoplus_cP_c\to(\bigoplus_cM_c)[0]$, a quasi-isomorphism by Step 2. Steps 7 and 8 identify $u_!(P)$ with $\bigoplus_cL_{uU_c}(P_c)$ and $u_!(a)$ with its augmentation to $(\bigoplus_cL_{uU_c}(M_c))[0]$, a quasi-isomorphism by Steps 4 and 2 on $\mathcal D$.

Canonical acyclicity. Take $V=C_{\mathcal E,R}$ or $V=u_!$. Both source and target are abelian by Step 1, the source has enough projectives by Step 5, and $V$ is additive and right exact by Step 8. The assumed total left derived functor is defined at every complex and has its canonical comparison. Step 9 gives a bounded above projective resolution $a:P\to T[0]$ for which $V(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The projective-computation clause of [lem-trf-bounded-above-acyclic-derived-computation] makes $\varepsilon_P$ invertible. Naturality of that canonical comparison gives
$\varepsilon_{T[0]}=Q(V(a))\,\varepsilon_P\,LV(Q(a))^{-1}$.
All three factors are invertible: $Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence the specific canonical comparison on $T[0]$ is invertible for each $V$, proving both acyclicity assertions. Finally repeat the same construction on $\mathcal D$ for the family $(uU_c,M_c)$ and $V=C_{\mathcal D,R}$. Step 8 identifies its sum with $u_!T$, so this also proves the stated left $C_{\mathcal D,R}$-acyclicity of $u_!T$.

lean.note: The declarations jointly state every clause. L_U, its evaluation adjunction, colimit, Kan extension, complexes and localization are existing Mathlib constructions.
